title: Gate finding
description: One finding observed by a station attempt (issue #1355, ADR-090). A finding is a subordinate process observation linked to the terminal event of its attempt — not a product Finding, not compliance evidence, and not a replacement for the ADR-029 issue record. The narrative stays on the issue thread; this carries only the bounded facts a yield/rework aggregate needs.

findingKey.description: Identity of this finding within its attempt. A source-provided stable key when one exists, otherwise an opaque deterministic digest of bounded structural fields. Never derived from prose, array position, or a timestamp, so a retry converges instead of appending a duplicate.

sourceId.description: Which reviewer or detector produced it: `core`, `security`, `test-quality` for reviewers; `sonarcloud`, `spotbugs`, `vale`, `policy`, `ci` for detectors. A non-review gate is never assigned a fabricated reviewer.

category.description: Source-native category: Sonar rule key, SpotBugs bug pattern, Vale check name, policy Violation.code, CI job/step name, or a review finding's category.shape. Absent when the source has none — a one-off review finding has no recurring shape, and a synthetic "uncategorized" would invent a category that does not exist. High-cardinality event data: never a metric label.

severity.description: Source-native severity, preserved exactly as the source expressed it. Absent when the source does not carry one — Codex core/security findings do not, and guessing would fabricate a distribution. Cross-station normalization requires separately versioned mapping data, never inference from title or reviewer identity.

SourceKind.description: Reviewers exercise judgement; detectors run a rule set. Keeping them distinct stops a scanner from being reported as a reviewer and vice versa.

Classification.description: The review envelope's own axis. Absent for detector findings, which do not classify this way.

Disposition.description: Detection and disposition are different moments. A newly detected finding is `open`; the terminal values are ADR-029's outcomes expressed as measurement facts. The review wrapper's pre-repair `decision: fix` is intent and must never be projected as `fixed`. A missing disposition is not `not-applicable` and is never counted as fixed.

x-ground-control-invariants.description: The schema admits no title, body, remediation text, file path, line number, raw tool output, or stack trace. A measurement projection that carried review prose would become a second durable record competing with ADR-029, and would leak source content into a reporting store.
Category, severity, and classification are optional, so a source that cannot attest one omits it rather than defaulting it to a value that would read as a real observation.

Disposition is a closed vocabulary whose terminal values match ADR-029's decision outcomes exactly, so measurement cannot grow a second disposition or deferral vocabulary. `defer` is absent by construction.
